source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary-source characterization of risk mitigation as 'API backward integration, dual sourcing, inventory buffers and process efficiency' — not explicitly framed as China+1 in accessible sources; primary AR/MD&A text could not be fetched directly (screener.in, sunpharma.com blocked in this environment).

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 press-release segment sales: India Formulations Rs 16,923 cr; US $1,921mn; Emerging Markets $1,114mn; RoW $847mn of total gross sales Rs 52,041 cr — export/USD-linked markets are the majority of non-India revenue. Third-party (MarketScreener) geography split: India 33%, US 31.3%, Other 35.7%, closely corroborating.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharma named among 55 firms selected for India's Rs 15,000 crore PLI scheme for the pharmaceutical sector (secondary source); company-specific incentive amount not quantified in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Lupin's API and CDMO businesses are aligned with global industry trends such as supply chain diversification, CDMO outsourcing, and high-potency APIs. Policies like the proposed Biosecure Act in the U.S., aimed at reducing dependency on China, are prompting global pharma players to diversify suppliers and invest in regional manufacturing hubs... Lupin has robust business contingency plans by way of alternate manufacturing sites and multiple API sources, which supports its diversification strategy.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company's risk management policy is to hedge above 15% of its estimated net foreign currency exposure in respect of highly probable forecast sales over the following 12-24 months at any point in time, using forward exchange contracts. Such contracts are generally designated as cash flow hedges, denominated in the same currency as the highly probable forecast sales with a hedge ratio of 1:1, and have a maturity of 12-24 months from the reporting date.
inr_exposure.evidence: The Company's risk management policy is to hedge above 15% of its estimated net foreign currency exposure in respect of highly probable forecasted sales over the following 12-24 months at any point in time... uses forward exchange contracts to hedge its currency risk.

rural.evidence: Rural and semi-urban markets are growing 1.5 times faster than the urban market (Pidilite MD commentary, FY25)

crude_exposure.evidence: VAM (vinyl acetate monomer), a crude-oil derivative, accounts for approximately 35-40% of Pidilite's raw material costs; management has repeatedly flagged VAM/crude-linked input cost volatility (e.g., a 40-50% VAM cost surge cited amid West Asia geopolitical tensions in one period, followed by moderation in another) as a key driver of gross margin movement.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Reported to mitigate imported raw material (VAM/petrochemical) cost and FX exposure via long-term supply contracts, hedging, and increasing local sourcing content; specific hedging instruments/percentages not confirmed from primary source.
inr_exposure.evidence: Pidilite mitigates supplier leverage via long-term contracts, hedging and approximately 60% local content in targeted products (secondary-source characterization, not a direct AR quote).

pli_scheme.evidence: Bosch is one of the companies that secured PLI approval under the 'Component Champion' category of the PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry (approved March 15, 2022, along with Sona BLW Precision, Delphi-TVS, Bharat Forge, Minda Corp, etc.); Bosch-specific revenue quantification not found in accessible sources.

rural.evidence: Growth has been broad-based, with Tier-II and III geographies growing faster than Tier-I

NIMF's AUM from 'Beyond the Top 30 cities' (B-30) stood at approx. Rs 1.32 trillion, forming 19.8% of NIMF's total AUM in FY2024-25, compared with 18.6% for the mutual fund industry (industry/AMFI-linked commentary via search, not directly verified against the AR PDF text).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported as near debt-free; third-party aggregators show total debt of roughly INR 880 million against equity of INR 42.1 billion (debt-to-equity ~2.1%), which for an AMC typically reflects Ind AS 116 lease liabilities rather than floating-rate borrowings.

inr_exposure.evidence: Operates overseas subsidiary Nippon Life India Asset Management (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. managing offshore/international advisory mandates, and has launched GIFT City feeder funds with Nissay Asset Management (Japan JV partner). No revenue % in USD or hedging policy disclosed/located for FY2024-25 specifically.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/broker commentary on NFIL's FY25 CDMO segment: "The company has gained from a trend in which pharmaceutical corporations shift some production to India rather than China"; NFIL has "entered into long-term supply contracts with certain South African miners for the supply of fluorspar, thus partially de-risking itself from China"; CDMO order book anchored by Fermion with an aspirational US$100m CDMO revenue target by FY27. Not independently verified against primary AR/MD&A text (nfil.in, BSE, broker PDFs blocked in this environment) — downgraded from 'strong' to 'moderate' pending primary-source confirmation.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Secondary sources indicate long-term debt of ~INR 10.7bn (Sep-2025) and that capex at subsidiary Navin Fluorine Advanced Sciences Ltd (Dahej MPP/AHF plant) is funded through a mix of debt and equity; Board also approved a fund-raising plan of up to Rs 750 crore via equity/GDR/ADR/FCCB. No floating-vs-fixed rate split located.

crude_exposure.evidence: Fluorspar (mined, not crude-derived) is the key raw material; third-party commentary notes chloromethanes and HF price increases on fluorspar/sulfuric-acid cost inflation, and that China controls a large share of global fluorspar/HF capacity. No company-disclosed % of crude/petrochemical-linked input cost was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports are USD/EUR-denominated via CDMO and specialty chemicals; three key customers (Bayer Crop Science, Corteva Agriscience, Fermion) reportedly account for a rising share of exports (to 80% in H1FY26 from 63% in FY24), implying growing concentrated foreign-currency revenue, but no specific hedging % or USD revenue share was located.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Torrent Pharma Inc. (US subsidiary) financial statements note term loans from banks carrying variable/floating interest rates, with average interest rate on borrowings at 6.26% for year ended 31 March 2024 vs 5.34% prior year; separately, ~Rs 12,500-14,000 crore of NCDs/commercial paper planned in 2025 to fund the JB Chemicals acquisition were priced at fixed rates of ~7.15-7.5%, alongside a ~Rs 20,000 crore bank credit line. Exact floating-rate share of total consolidated debt not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company discloses geographic revenue mix (India 55%, Brazil 10%, US 10%, Germany 10%, other international markets 15% for FY2024-25) implying meaningful USD/EUR/BRL revenue exposure, but specific consolidated USD-revenue % and forex hedging policy details were not found in accessible sources.

rural.evidence: Company commentary describes a pan-India distribution network with emphasis on semi-urban and rural penetration, citing rising rural incomes, population growth, and conversion from illicit/toddy liquor to IMFL as rural demand drivers; also serves price-sensitive rural consumers via its country liquor business. No quantified rural revenue % was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw material cost pressure is attributed to grain and ENA (extra neutral alcohol) price inflation, not crude oil; grain price inflation reportedly had a ~490 bps negative YoY impact on gross margin in FY2024, offset by premiumization and price increases. No crude-oil-linked packaging cost quantification was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports to 100+ countries reportedly contributed approximately 9% of revenue in FY25; no specific USD hedging policy disclosure was found.

govt_capex.evidence: Sector commentary cited in IHCL communications: 'favourable demographics, increasing employment, higher disposable income of a young middle class, robust domestic demand, increased investments and improving infrastructure and connectivity' with a projected INR 2,000 crore government allocation for tourism infrastructure development in 2024-25, plus IHCL's active support of the government's 'Dekho Apna Desh' domestic-travel campaign and benefit from UDAN airport-connectivity expansion; no company-specific revenue % tied to this was disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: IHCL reported becoming debt-free as of 31 March 2025, with nil net debt, a gross cash position of INR 3,073 crores, and old term loans/GECL loans taken during Covid fully repaid; interest coverage ratio improved to 13.4x (FY25) from 8.6x (FY24). No specific floating-vs-fixed rate borrowing mix % was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: IHCL's operations span four continents and ~14 countries/150+ locations; FY25 saw 20% growth in the US portfolio (part of the international/New Businesses segment, which drove much of the gap between standalone revenue of ~INR 5,145 crore and consolidated revenue of INR 8,565 crore). No explicit USD-denominated revenue % or forex hedging policy disclosure was located.

china_plus_one.evidence: "We are well-placed to benefit from the shifts in the new trade policies, and we firmly believe that today's disruptions will eventually lead to consolidation around companies with strong technological moats... As global supply chains continue to diversify, our strong alignment with India's industrial growth becomes increasingly evident." Also: 'Amid geopolitical instability and global trade restrictions...the Company swiftly activated contingency plans...It diversified sourcing and logistics strategies, established alternative shipping routes.' Company secured net order book of INR 242 billion (USD 2.8bn), 77% from EV programmes, with 4 new EV programmes and 2 new EV customers won in FY25 (FY2024-25 Annual Report, Chairman's message / CFO review).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Notes to standalone financial statements, Interest rate risk exposure: Variable rate borrowings INR 134.63 million vs Fixed rate borrowings INR 0.00 million as at 31st March 2025 (Total borrowings INR 134.63 million) — i.e., all disclosed borrowings are variable/floating rate.

crude_exposure.evidence: Material cost accounted for 43% of total income in both FY 2024-25 and FY 2023-24, but is predominantly metal-linked (special steel alloy bars, iron castings, steel forgings, copper enamelled wires, machined aluminium die castings, bearings, magnets) with only minor plastic-moulded-component content — not a crude-oil-indexed raw material base, so left null for this signal rather than reporting the 43% total material cost figure.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Board-approved hedging policy primarily using forward contracts to hedge currency risk; natural/partial hedge via geographically diversified manufacturing (India, Mexico, USA, Serbia, China plants).
inr_exposure.evidence: "Your Company operates internationally, and a large portion of the business is transacted in international currencies primarily in US$ and EUR... exposed to foreign exchange risk through our sales and services in the USA, Europe, China and other countries... carries out currency hedging based upon a Board approved hedging policy which primarily employs forward contracts." Outstanding forward contracts as at 31 March 2025: USD 109.55 million (receivable), EUR 20.81 million (receivable), JPY 97.37 million (payable), EUR 8.00 million (payable).

pli_scheme.evidence: CFO's Review, FY2024-25 Annual Report: "We benefited from income accrual from the Auto PLI scheme, for which we had eight products approved, and from deploying surplus funds in various investments." No separate quantified PLI income/revenue % was disclosed in the Other Income note breakdown.

china_plus_one.evidence: Alkem Activa (Alkem's API arm) operates 2 USFDA-approved API manufacturing facilities in India plus 1 in the US, offering ~33 commercial APIs with US-DMF filings and ~11 under development — indicating backward integration reducing reliance on imported (incl. Chinese) APIs/KSMs. No explicit 'China+1' language was found in accessible AR/MD&A excerpts; this is inferred from subsidiary capability disclosures, not a directly quoted management narrative.

rural.evidence: Secondary commentary indicates Alkem leveraged its acute-therapy/anti-infective leadership to expand into trade generics (a distributor-led model) that gained traction in Tier 2/3 towns during and after Covid, capturing volume gains as affordability improves across rural and urban India. No quantified rural/semi-urban revenue percentage was found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Alkem is a low-leverage/net-cash company (reported net cash position ~INR 5,474 crore per FY26-era disclosures; debt-to-equity ~0.33 in FY23). No specific floating-rate-debt percentage was found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: CFO (Nitin Agrawal) has stated the company hedges approximately 80% of its forex exposure.
inr_exposure.evidence: "Alkem Laboratories hedges 80% of its forex exposure" — per CFO commentary; international sales (predominantly USD-linked, comprising US at 19.4% and other international markets at 10.5% of FY25 revenue) total ~29.8% of consolidated revenue.

Secondary-source (aggregator) data classify FY2024-25 revenue as ~100% International (predominantly USA) / 0% Domestic (India); no primary annual-report quote on hedging policy or exact geographic split (US vs. Canada/Australia) could be retrieved (screener.in, ikshealth.com/investor-relations, and RHP/DRHP PDFs blocked in this environment).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Analyst summaries describe Ajanta Pharma as 'almost debt-free,' implying minimal exposure to floating-rate borrowings, but no quantified floating-rate liability % was located.

inr_exposure.evidence: Search-derived analyst commentary references a 'forex derivative loss of Rs 37 crore included in other expenses,' suggesting the company uses forex derivatives/hedging, but the primary Notes to Accounts (financial risk management section) could not be accessed to confirm USD revenue % or the exact hedging policy.

govt_capex.evidence: International markets accounted for 55% of total revenues in FY25, reflecting sustained demand in sectors such as oil and gas, mining, and infrastructure; company capex focused on 'value-added steel solutions and wire rope innovations for global infrastructure, mining, and construction sectors.'

rate_sensitive.evidence: Consolidated net debt reduced to Rs. 63 crore in FY25 despite Rs. 245 crore of capex during the year; specific floating-vs-fixed rate debt split not found in accessible sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Oil & gas appears only as a demand-side end-market (e.g., oil country tubular goods, rig wire ropes), not as a raw material input; raw materials are steel/iron-ore/coking-coal linked. No crude-oil raw-material linkage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export/international revenue is 55% of FY25 total revenue, but no explicit USD-denomination % or hedging/forward-contract policy could be retrieved from accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Secondary-source summary indicates 'Usha Martin benefits from the PLI scheme continuity for its Steel Wire Ropes and Wire Products operations,' consistent with steel wires being a covered category under India's Specialty Steel PLI scheme; could not be cross-verified against the official approved-applicants list or the company's own AR disclosure.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company disclosures describe in-house API manufacturing facilities (Vizag and Hyderabad) providing backward integration for products where external API supply is uncertain, giving better control of the supply chain and cost efficiencies; no explicit language quantifying reduced dependence on Chinese API sourcing was found (parent Fosun Pharma is itself China-based, and no distinct 'de-risking from China' MD&A narrative was located).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Third-party financial data aggregators describe Gland Pharma as 'almost debt free'; exact floating-rate borrowings disclosure from Notes to financial statements could not be verified from primary source.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 consolidated revenue of Rs 56,165 million was ~95.6% export-driven (USA ~54.1%, Europe/Cenexi ~29.3%, Canada/ANZ+RoW ~13.2%), indicating majority foreign-currency (largely USD) revenue exposure; exact disclosed USD-revenue percentage and hedging/forward-contract policy language from Notes to Accounts could not be verified from primary source.

rural.evidence: B-30 (beyond top-30 cities) Monthly AAUM grew 34% YoY to Rs 711 billion in Q2 FY25, accounting for ~18% of Mutual Fund AUM (17.7% in Q1 FY25); full-year FY24-25 annual report figure not independently confirmed as the AR PDF was inaccessible.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is near debt-free; 5-year average debt-to-equity ratio ~2.44% vs industry average ~1.92% (likely lease liabilities only, per AMC-industry norm); no specific floating-rate borrowing breakdown found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Operates a GIFT City (IFSC) branch offering offshore AIFs/PMS in USD, e.g. ABSL Global Emerging Market Equity Fund (IFSC) closed at $69.89 million and ABSL India Growth Fund AIF raised USD 70 million; these are USD-denominated AUM raises, not disclosed as a % of company revenue, so no revenue-linked figure could be extracted.
